why_seated: THE REPORTS. Platonic Questions 8.1 (1006C): Theophrastus reports that Plato, grown older, repented of giving the earth the middle place, which did not befit it; the same Question reads the Timaeus's winding earth as the earth Aristarchus and Seleucus later showed turning. Numa 11: the Pythagorean central fire called Hestia, the earth not of the most honoured parts, and Plato grown old said to think the same. De facie 6 (923A): Cleanthes held that the Greeks should indict Aristarchus for impiety, as moving the hearth (Hestia) of the cosmos.
verified_loci: Plat. Q. 8.1, 1006C, Plato's repentance on Theophrastus's word — 'Θεόφραστος δὲ καὶ προσιστορεῖ τῷ Πλάτωνι πρεσβυτέρῳ γενομένῳ μεταμέλειν' (text/tlg0007.tlg133.perseus-grc2.txt)
Plat. Q. 8.1, Aristarchus and Seleucus — 'Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σέλευκος ἀπεδείκνυσαν' (text/tlg0007.tlg133.perseus-grc2.txt)
Numa 11, the earth not of the most honoured parts — 'οὐ τῶν τιμιωτάτων οὐδὲ τῶν πρώτων τοῦ κόσμου μορίων' (text/tlg0007.tlg005.perseus-grc2.txt)
De facie 923A, Cleanthes against Aristarchus — 'ὥσπερ Ἀρίσταρχον ᾤετο δεῖν Κλεάνθης τὸν Σάμιον ἀσεβείας προσκαλεῖσθαι τοὺς Ἕλληνας' (text/tlg0007.tlg126.perseus-grc2.txt)
